description:
We are Colombian computer science students. Members of the Center for Innovation and Artificial Intelligence at our university, UTS, we are interested in learning more and creating new technology applications to contribute to science.

Participating in this hackathon allows us to put our knowledge into practice and improve it, as well as identify our weaknesses and strengthen them so that we can achieve great projects.
summary: An interactive platform designed to improve fire safety research in microgravity and future space habitats. Our solution transforms NASA's official PSI combustion research data into an accessible and interactive knowledge platform and users can discover experiments, compare combustion conditions, analyze datasets, and identify relevant safety insights.
details:
It combines Artificial Intelligence (AI), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and a cloud-based architecture to help users explore, retrieve, analyze, and compare combustion experiments. A key feature is its data traceability approach, which connects AI-assisted insights directly to official NASA sources, reducing the risk of hallucinations and unsupported information.

The platform includes several interactive modules:

  • Dashboard: Provides an overview of the platform and its research data.
  • Discover: Allows users to explore combustion experiments and scientific records.
  • Ranking: Organizes relevant research records according to their characteristics.
  • Compare: Enables comparisons between experiments and combustion conditions.
  • Data Lab: Facilitates scientific data exploration and analysis.
  • Safety Insights: Highlights relevant findings related to fire safety in space.
  • AI Assistant: An intelligent conversational assistant that allows users to ask questions about combustion research and receive answers based on the information available within the platform, connecting responses to relevant scientific sources.
  • Official Sources Repository: Provides access to NASA research, historical missions, and PSI datasets.

Fire behaves differently in microgravity because the absence of buoyancy-driven convection changes flame shape and propagation. This makes traditional terrestrial fire models insufficient for fully understanding combustion in space. These challenges are especially relevant for future lunar and Martian habitats, where atmospheric composition and oxygen concentration may increase fire risks.

CombusLab makes scientific information easier to access, explore, and compare. Its main benefits include improving access to NASA research, supporting evidence-based analysis, reducing AI hallucinations through source traceability, and helping users identify relevant information for future fire prevention strategies.

During development, our team considered scientific accuracy, the unique behavior of fire in microgravity, the atmospheric challenges of future lunar and Martian habitats, data accessibility, AI reliability, user experience, and the practical application of research findings like safer human space exploration.

We used:

1. Design and Creative Tools

  • Pixilart: Used to create the project's icon and visual elements for the AI assistant.
  • Canva: Used to create the presentation slides and develop the initial visual design and identity of the project.

2. Artificial Intelligence and Development Tools

Gemini, ChatGPT, OpenAI Codex, Google Antigravity, Groq, Pollinations AI and Cloudflare Workers AI

3. Programming Languages

  • Python: 7.5%
  • TypeScript: 7.1%
  • JavaScript: 2.3%
